title: Lingguang's open ecosystem continues to expand, adding multiple service connections including WeChat Reading, Quark, Hello Ride, McDonald's, and more
excerpt: On November 4, Ant Lingguang received a new round of upgrades, adding connector services such as podcast subscriptions, Quark Cloud Drive, Hello Taxi, McDonald'
content_html:
On November 4, Ant Lingguang received a new round of upgrades, adding connector services such as podcast subscriptions, Quark Cloud Drive, Hello Taxi, McDonald's, and WeChat Reading, extending its capabilities to more everyday scenarios including information management, content subscriptions, fitness and reading, and lifestyle consumption. Prior to this, Lingguang had already integrated connector services such as Alipay, NetEase Mail, and Feishu. With this, 40 external connectors have now been connected under Lingguang's open ecosystem.

As AI assistants can connect to more and more external services, their value is beginning to show in cross-tool, cross-scenario task management capabilities. As a personal AI assistant that can get things done, Lingguang's latest upgrade further reflects this trend.

On the content consumption side, the addition of podcast subscriptions, an RSS reader, and WeChat Reading allows users to continuously obtain and manage information around personal interests; on the life services side, the integration of services such as Hello Taxi and McDonald's further extends the Agent's capabilities to travel and daily consumption.

These services may seem scattered, but together they point to one change: the boundary of AI capabilities is expanding from a single digital tool to continuous management in users' real lives.

Based on the classification of Lingguang user requests, finance and consumption scenarios accounted for 23.83%, while health and habits scenarios accounted for 21.46%. This means users are turning AI from a general Q&A tool into a service entry point for handling personal finance, health management, and daily affairs.

For example, in financial scenarios, users want the Agent to help sort out bills and analyze spending structure; in health management, users check workout data and adjust diet plans; in work and family life, email follow-ups, calendar reminders, and to-do management are also gradually becoming real needs.

More notably, the requests users make to Lingguang are also getting closer to how work is done in real life. Users are beginning to ask AI not only to understand instructions, but also to understand relationships between tasks and to keep paying attention to and tracking subsequent execution status.

In travel scenarios, needs are no longer limited to checking routes or recommending transportation modes; they extend further to requests such as "book me a ride in 10 minutes" and "keep an eye on my discounted express ride order." Such requests involve not only immediate actions but also scheduling and ongoing tasks such as tracking order status. In learning and personal productivity scenarios, users may make requests such as "move the other course tasks later" and "has the completion status been synced?"

It is understood that Lingguang is a personal AI assistant developed by Ant Group. It officially launched on November 18, 2025, and surpassed 2 million downloads within six days. On October 27, 2026, Lingguang 2.0 was officially released, driving the AI assistant from a "task executor" to an "affairs manager."
